numbering_direction.summary: SECTION NUMBERS INCREASE TOWARD THIRD BASE / LEFT FIELD (and decrease toward first base / right field). On the 100 level the run starts at 101 in right-center field, sweeps 101->106 across right field, 107-111 around the right-field foul pole (Kaline's Corner), 112-117 up the right-field/first-base line, 118-137 through the infield (home plate at 127-128), 138-143 down the third-base/left-field line, and 144-151 across left field. The 200 level (mezzanine, 210-219) and the 300 level (321-346) follow the SAME rotational direction: 210 nearest right field -> 219 nearest home plate; 321 on the first-base side -> 327-328 behind home plate -> 337 toward third base -> 338-346 down the left-field line, ending with 344-346 deep in left field. Equivalently: viewed on a standard seating map with home plate at the bottom, numbers ascend counter-clockwise... i.e. from the right-field side of the map, across the top of home plate, and out to left field.

accessibility.summary: Wheelchair-accessible and companion seating is distributed throughout the ballpark on all three levels. Official language: 'Wheelchair accessible sections are located throughout all areas of the ballpark' with unobstructed field views on the 100, 200 and 300 levels. Companion seats are sold alongside each accessible seat. Purchase: any box office window before game day, the customer service window on game day, by phone at 313-471-BALL, or at tigers.com; ticket exchanges for mobility accommodations are handled at box office windows on game day subject to availability and possible upgrade charges. Service animals are permitted; the pet relief area is outside the Rocket Entry at Grand Circus Park. ROW-LABEL TELL: accessible/ADA rows in the seating manifest carry an 'AC' suffix and appear ABOVE the lettered rows at the entry-tunnel level - e.g. row 'DAC' in sections 333, 337, 343 (above Row C), row 'TAC' in section 148, row 'HHAC' in section 144. Treat any row ending in 'AC' as the wheelchair/companion platform row for that section.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: MIXED - Comerica Park uses BOTH letters and numbers for rows, and many sections use both in sequence. There is no single park-wide convention. Patterns observed on RateYourSeats section pages (all verbatim): (1) Infield-box sections run lettered PREMIUM rows first, then numbered rows - Section 126: 'Rows in Section 126 are labeled HHH-KKK, 15-35'; Section 129 and 130: same 'HHH-KKK, 15-35'; Section 125: 'HHH-KKK, 15-35'. The triple-letter rows HHH-KKK are the Priority Club rows; the numbered rows 1-13 in front of them are the On-Deck Circle rows. (2) Some 100-level sections are PURELY NUMBERED - Section 135: 'Rows in Section 135 are labeled 7-35'; Section 140: 'Rows in Section 140 are labeled 1-35'; Section 110: 'Rows in Section 110 are labeled 21-36'; Section 115: 'Rows in Section 115 are labeled 27-47'; Section 120: 'Rows 7-35'. (3) Outfield sections are PURELY LETTERED or letter-run - Section 101: 'Rows in Section 101 are labeled E-T'; Section 148: 'Rows in Section 148 are labeled A-S, TAC, AA-HH'; Section 144: 'Rows in Section 144 are labeled A-Z, AA-GG, HHAC'. (4) 200 level - Section 212: 'Rows in Section 212 are labeled A-F, 1-22'. (5) 300 level is uniformly LETTERS THEN NUMBERS - 'Rows in Section 326 are labeled A-F, 1-20' (also 321, 322, 330, 331, 332, 338, 340, 341, 345, 346); sections with an ADA row read 'A-C, DAC, 1-20' (sections 333, 337, 343). Rows A-F on the 300 level are the Upper Box Club Seats. Rows 15 and above on the 300 level are covered by the overhang. SUMMARY RULE: expect lettered rows for premium/front-of-section and outfield seating and numbered rows for standard bowl seating; any row token ending in 'AC' (DAC, TAC, HHAC) is an ADA/accessible platform row.
discovery.seat1_side_verbatim: "When looking towards the field/stage, lower number seats are on the right"
discovery._seat1_notes: This exact sentence appears identically on EVERY Comerica Park section page checked - 101, 110, 115, 120, 125, 126, 129, 130, 135, 140, 144, 148, 212, 321, 322, 323, 326, 328, 330, 331, 332, 333, 337, 338, 340, 341, 343, 345, 346 - so it is a park-wide rule, not a per-section one. Interpretation: SEAT 1 IS ON THE RIGHT-HAND SIDE OF THE SECTION AS YOU FACE THE FIELD (equivalently, on your left as you look from the field back into the stands). Because section numbers increase toward third base/left field, seat 1 of a given section is therefore on that section's LOWER-SECTION-NUMBER edge - i.e. seat numbers, like section numbers, ascend in the first-base/right-field -> third-base/left-field direction. CONFIRMED. Source: https://www.rateyourseats.com/comerica-park/seating/sections/135 (and every other section page).
discovery.known_obstructions: Comerica Park is generally marketed as obstruction-free - ballparksofbaseball.com states there are 'No obstructed views' across the facility - but several real quirks exist: (1) UPPER-DECK FRONT-ROW RAILINGS/PLEXIGLASS. Fan review on the Section 328 page, verbatim: 'These seats are OBSTRUCTED by the railings and the plexiglass. You would have to be way over 6 feet tall to see over these.' This applies to the front lettered rows (A-F) of the 300-level Upper Box Club sections generally, not just 328. (2) PROTECTIVE NETTING. Official: the net 'runs from behind home plate through section 116 down the First Base line, and section 142 on the Third Base line' - everything inside 116-142 views the field through netting (the Tigers describe it as 'among the most transparent in all of baseball'). (3) RIGHT-FIELD BLEACHER SIGHTLINE. Section 101 (right-center bleachers) can lose a portion of the outfield / the right-field corner from view. (4) MEZZANINE OVERHANG. The 200-level mezzanine overhangs the last ~10 rows of 100-level sections 112-117, cutting off high fly balls (and providing the park's best shade). (5) SCOREBOARD SIGHTLINES. The main scoreboard is in LEFT field, so 100-level sections 138-143 and upper sections 341-346 must turn around to see it; upper sections 321-324 and 338-340 have the easiest looks. (6) SUN. The third-base side and the left-field bleachers get the most direct sun; the first-base side (100 sections 112-127 upper rows, all of 210-219, upper 321-330) is the shaded side. UNCERTAIN: no source found enumerating specific pole/support obstructions.

The DERIVED facts (home plate at the north end, first-base side = west, third-base side = east, right field = southwest, left field = southeast) are cross-confirmed by gate geography, sun behavior, and the Ferris wheel / carousel corner descriptions, and should be treated as reliable.
